requests.problem: WS03 verifies KO1298 passwords with a 12-byte wire maximum while current WS13 validation accepts 10-128 characters. Frontend-only rejection is not an authoritative production boundary.
requests.required_change: At register, password change, and password-reset confirm, enforce the agreed shared KO1298-compatible credential envelope server-side before hashing. The password must be evaluated exactly as submitted; do not trim, truncate, normalize, transliterate, or silently transform it. Publish the exact byte encoding/charset semantics in the WS13 contract and cover boundary tests including 9, 10, 12, 13 bytes and multibyte input.
requests.frontend_interim: The official website restricts newly created/replaced passwords to a conservative 10-12 printable-ASCII-character subset so each character is one byte. Existing login/current-password fields are not rewritten or truncated.
acceptance: WS13 rejects any new credential outside the shared game-compatible byte envelope.
WS13 OpenAPI/README describe byte/charset semantics rather than only 10-128 characters.
Register -> verify -> website login -> WS03 game login succeeds with the same raw password.
No password transformation occurs in frontend, WS13, persistence, or WS03 verification.

requests.problem: Current verification/reset delivery exceptions are audited but swallowed, while the public request still returns accepted. A frontend cannot truthfully distinguish successful delivery from delivery failure.
requests.required_change: Provide a production-safe way to establish delivery readiness/outcome without exposing reset/verification tokens or enabling account enumeration. This may be an operational readiness contract plus durable delivery queue semantics; the public response must remain enumeration-safe.
requests.frontend_interim: The website says only that the request was accepted and that the delivery service will send a code when the account/state matches. It never says that an email was definitely sent and never displays a token.
acceptance: Production deployment can prove verification/reset delivery is configured and healthy.
Delivery failures are observable to operations without token leakage.
